rule: Balance responsive pointer location with smooth physical force; test both rawness and lag.
why: Reasonable smoothing values can feel smudged or inconsistent with a control's state.
mechanism: Immediate acknowledgement with spatially coupled response and controlled force/settle.
whenToUse: Pointer-driven environmental response or direct manipulation.
whenNotToUse: Touch/no-pointer paths; essential actions must not depend on pointer precision.
parameters: Position, force, activation and state timing need independent contextual tuning.
No universal millisecond value is encoded.
dependencies: Pointer entry/leave/blur handling and keyboard/touch alternatives.
implementationPattern: Separate location response from force activation if their jobs differ.
Initialize inactive-to-active location at entry; release pressure on leave/blur.
Use elapsed time rather than frame-count damping.

goodExample.claim: LAMELLA Human Review described natural, responsive pointer and useful click response.

antiExample.claim: Original VELORUM pointer could feel smudged in intense regions.

tests: Slow/fast travel, sudden reversal, stop, leave/re-enter and dense graphical regions.
Compare location and force after state change; test reduced motion and touch alternative.
repairStrategy: For lag, shorten location response and reduce trails before shrinking semantic force.
For rawness, add minimal time-correct response or controlled force onset.
Re-test human feel after tuning; an error measurement cannot certify UX.
cost: A few state values; pointer effects themselves may have renderer cost.

provenance.claim: Candidate operationalization of existing human/technical experiment evidence; transfer unvalidated.
HEG/TEG specification and Human Authority boundary.

transferability: Observed context only; weaker-model and cross-domain transfer TO VALIDATE.
